Los contrastes no paramétricos no usan l: Non-parametric tests do not use the values but their order (the ranks). That is why they do not need the data to be normal and are hardly affected by outliers, at the cost of having slightly less power if the data were in fact normal.
Se ordenan juntos todos los datos y se s: All the data are ordered together and the ranks of each sample are added, $R_1$ and $R_2$. $U_1 = R_1 − n_1(n_1 + 1)/2$ counts how many times a data point of sample 1 exceeds one of sample 2 (ties count half), and $U_1 + U_2 = n_1 n_2$. It tests whether one sample tends to give larger values than the other.
Se toman las diferencias $d_i$ (entre la: The differences $d_i$ are taken (between the two measurements or with respect to the median of $H_0$), the zero ones are discarded, the $|d_i|$ are ranked and the ranks of the positive ones, $W^+$, and of the negative ones, $W^−$, are added. If $H_0$ is true, both sums are similar.
Es el ANOVA de un factor con rangos. Se: It is the one-way ANOVA with ranks. All the data are ordered together and we check whether the mean ranks of the groups differ more than expected: $H = {12}/{N(N + 1)} ∑ {R_i^2}/{n_i} − 3(N + 1)$, divided by the tie correction $1 − {∑ (t^3 − t)}/{N^3 − N}$, follows approximately a $χ^2$ with $k − 1$ degrees of freedom. If it is significant, Dunn's comparisons say which pairs differ: $z = {R̄_i − R̄_j}/√({N(N + 1)}/12 · (1/n_i + 1/n_j))$ with the p-value adjusted by Holm (more powerful) or Bonferroni. The effect size is $ε^2 = H/(N − 1)$.
El más sencillo: solo cuenta si cada dif: The simplest: it only counts whether each difference is positive or negative. If $H_0$ is true, $n^+$ is a binomial $B(n, 1/2)$ and the p-value is exact. It uses less information than Wilcoxon (it ignores how much), so it has less power, but it asks almost nothing of the data.
Miden si dos variables crecen juntas aun: They measure whether two variables grow together even if not in a straight line. Spearman is the Pearson correlation of the ranks. Kendall counts concordant ($C$) and discordant ($D$) pairs: $τ_b = (C − D)/√((n_0 − n_1)(n_0 − n_2))$; its p-value is exact without ties and is more reliable with little data.
El p-valor no dice cuánto. Para Mann-Whi: The p-value does not say how much. For Mann-Whitney the probability of superiority $U_1/(n_1 n_2)$ is given (0.5 if there is no difference) and $r = |z|/√N$ (0.1 small, 0.3 medium, 0.5 large). The Hodges-Lehmann estimator is the median of all the differences between a data point of one sample and one of the other (in Wilcoxon, of the Walsh averages $(d_i + d_j)/2$), with its confidence interval, the same one given by R's wilcox.test.
